question: Can benchmarks be kept informative if data are collected dynamically, with humans and state-of-the-art models in the loop over multiple rounds, instead of as static datasets that saturate?
hypothesis: We can make even faster progress if we evaluate models and collect data dynamically, with humans and models in the loop, rather than the traditional static way.
contributions: Dynabench, an open-source web platform for human-and-model-in-the-loop dataset creation and model benchmarking
Four initial official tasks (NLI, QA, sentiment, hate speech) with multi-round data
A discussion of objections to dynamic benchmarking and future goals

method.summary: A web platform where annotators write examples intended to fool a target model served live (TorchServe), with other humans validating the examples; collection proceeds in rounds, with models retrained between rounds. Position paper with a progress report on four tasks.
method.task: dynamic adversarial data collection and benchmarking (NLI, extractive QA, sentiment, hate speech)

datasets.source: Bartolo et al. 2020; Wikipedia contexts identical to SQuAD1.1

limits: Position paper plus progress report: no controlled experiments, no per-round accuracy tables, no hyperparameters or seeds.
Authors concede unnatural distributions, annotator overfitting to the model in the loop, dependence on the target model, and no guarantees for future models not in the loop.
Only classification and span-extraction tasks, English text only; generative tasks left to future work.
Dynamic benchmarks cost more and benchmark comparability across changing rounds is the main adoption hurdle.
Numbers are from 2021 and Table 1 statistics are a snapshot.
